subs_mobile_path.source: House forecast, end-of-year mobile subscribers ('000): H2-2026 recovery of +170k from the Q2 trough (gross adds still below pre-conflict per the company's own Q2 commentary), then +310k/+250k/+230k/+210k as tourism and population inflows normalise — well below the +788k of boom-year 2025, above the flat conflict quarter

subs_fixed_path.source: House forecast, end-of-year fixed subscribers ('000): +16k in H2-2026 then +30k/+25k/+23k/+20k — continued fibre/FWA share gain at a slowing rate; FY2025 added +53k

arpu_mobile_path.source: House forecast, blended mobile ARPU AED/month: held essentially flat (+0.3%/yr) — postpaid mix gain (+9% y/y postpaid growth) offsetting prepaid dilution; company printed 63.3-63.4 across FY2025-Q2-2026

arpu_fixed_path.source: House forecast, implied fixed revenue per subscriber AED/month (fixed segment revenue / average base — a blend of consumer broadband and enterprise fixed, so a revenue-intensity metric, not a tariff): H1-2026 actual 533; FY2025 515. +1.5%/yr on enterprise/ICT-adjacent mix

seg_g.source: House forecast: wholesale −0.8% in 2026 (H1 actual −2.0% y/y on conflict-hit roaming/transit, partial H2 stabilisation) then +1.5-2%; ICT +7.9% in 2026 (H1 actual +4.8%, Q4-heavy seasonality) accelerating to +11% on the data-centre ramp (Microsoft hyperscale agreement, du Q4-2025 deck) then easing to +8%

contrib_margin_path.source: Segment contribution margins: mobile/fixed/wholesale held at the audited FY2025 rates (60.8% / 85.8% / 86.4% — FY2024: 60.9% / 84.6% / 88.0%); ICT lifted 19.4% -> 21.5% over five years on data-centre scale (still the thinnest-margin segment)

opex_base_fy25.source: Audited consolidated FS, Integrated Annual Report 2025, investors.du.ae (KPMG Lower Gulf, unmodified opinion 09-Feb-2026), face of the income statement: net operating expenses before D&A by nature (licence = telecommunication licence and related fees, a revenue-linked regulatory charge; ecl = impairment of trade/lease receivables and contract assets net of recoveries)

esc_staff.source: Staff-cost escalator 2.0%/yr — UAE wage inflation proxied by CPI (~2%) on a base the company is actively managing DOWN (H1-2026 staff cost −6.3% y/y, reviewed interims); applied from a rebased FY2026 level

esc_network.source: Network & maintenance escalator 3.0%/yr — grows with network scale (sites, fibre, data centres), proxied by blended subscriber growth plus capacity additions

esc_admin.source: Administrative escalator 2.0%/yr — general UAE cost inflation

marketing_pct.source: Marketing at 1.80% of revenue (FY2025 actual 1.84%, H1-2026 1.44% — conflict-quarter restraint; forecast between the two)

licence_pct.source: Telecom licence and related fees at 2.70% of revenue (FY2025 2.73%, H1-2026 2.65% — a regulatory revenue-share, so revenue-linked by its own nature)

ecl_pct.source: Expected-credit-loss charge at 1.45% of revenue (FY2025 1.33%, H1-2026 1.64% — conflict-quarter receivables stress; forecast between the two)

staff_fy26.source: FY2026E staff cost: H1-2026 actual 471.360 + H2 at the H2-2025 seasonal ratio (H2 runs above H1; 513.6 = H1 x 1.09) — the company's own run-rate after the efficiency program, escalated 2%/yr thereafter

other_inc_path.source: Other operating income held at AED 15mn/yr (FY2025 21.7, H1-2026 5.8 — lumpy, small)

capex_pct.source: Capex (PP&E + intangibles, cash basis) / revenue: FY2025 actual 14.8% (2,353.230 / 15,905.421, audited CF); H1-2026 12.7% with the company stating a back-loaded, data-centre-heavy plan and commitments UP at 2,411.760 (30-Jun-26 note) vs 2,124.526 (FY2025) — 15.5% at the peak of the data-centre build, gliding to 13.0% (no numeric company capex guidance for FY2026 was published; flagged as a house path on sourced commitment evidence)

capex_tang_share.source: Tangible share of capex: FY2025 audited 2,038.501 / 2,353.230

dep_rate_ppe.source: PP&E depreciation rate on OPENING gross-of-additions balance: FY2025 audited PP&E depreciation 1,557.989 / opening PP&E 9,838.448 = 15.83%

amort_rate.source: Intangibles amortisation rate on opening balance: FY2025 amortisation 245.881 / opening intangibles 846.932 = 29.0% (short-lived software; the TDRA licence is fully amortised at NBV 0.869)

rou_dep_path.source: Right-of-use depreciation: FY2025 actual 364.063, FY2024 374.505, FY2023 445.042 — a gently declining site-lease book; held on that glide. Lease REPLACEMENT capex is set equal to ROU depreciation in the FCFF build (the steady-state assumption; actual FY2025 lease additions were only 96.034, so this is the conservative side)

rf.source: AED risk-free anchor: UAE federal AED T-bond, January-2031 tranche, auction yield 4.48% (22-Jul-2026 auction, +4bp over matched UST) - the longest LIQUID recent AED government primary print. There is no liquid 10-year AED point (longest AED primary ever is the Feb-2033 tranche at 4.13%, Apr-2026, now stale); the 10-year peg-extrapolated alternative (Abu Dhabi USD 10y 4.73% Feb-2026 less the ~4bp AED-through-USD basis ~= 4.69%) is carried as rf_alt and PRICED in section 1.8 rather than averaged in

lens_weights.source: House synthesis weights, operating-company pattern (SWDY reference study)

g_term.source: Terminal nominal AED growth 2.5%: below the IMF's UAE long-run nominal GDP growth (~4%: real ~4% + CPI ~2% per WEO Apr-2026) and consistent with a mature duopoly telecom growing at population-plus-inflation minus price erosion

rf_alt.source: Peg-extrapolated 10-year AED proxy: Abu Dhabi sovereign USD 10-year 4.73% (Feb-2026 issue, UST+25bp) less ~4bp observed AED-through-USD basis at matched tenor. The priced alternative construction for the risk-free tenor gap

sov_spread_rating.source: Damodaran ctryprem dataset (05-Jan-2026 update), United Arab Emirates row: Moody's Aa2, rating-based adjusted default spread 0.42%

erp_rating.source: Damodaran ctryprem (05-Jan-2026): UAE total equity risk premium 4.87% = 4.23% mature-market base + 0.64% country risk premium (rating basis). This is ERP basis 1

sov_spread_mkt.source: Market-spread basis: Abu Dhabi USD 10-year traded at UST+25bp (Feb-2026 issue; UAE CDS itself unreachable - cbonds 403, Damodaran shows NA for UAE CDS; failure logged, never substituted silently). Basis-2 default spread = 0.25%

erp_mkt.source: ERP basis 2 (market-spread, fresher base): Damodaran live implied US ERP 4.28% (01-Aug-2026, T12m adjusted payout) + CRP scaled off the market default spread 0.25% x 1.52 (Damodaran's own CRP/spread multiple 0.64/0.42) = 0.38% -> 4.66%. Same-basis consistency: this WACC strips the 0.25% market spread from rf, never the 0.42% rating spread

beta.source: Tier-1 own-stock regression: DU weekly log-returns vs the DFM General Index (official DFM API spliced with cross-validated Yahoo DFMGI.AE; identical closes on all 307 overlapping sessions), 5-year window, last-common-session weekly sampling: beta 0.472, R2 0.202, n 259, SE 0.058, CI90 [0.38, 0.57] - passes the usability gate (n>=24, R2>=5%, SE<|beta|). Equal-weight AE-library composite cross-check: 0.394 (R2 0.118). A defensive, negative-net-debt telecom regressing below 0.5 on its own index is economically coherent; betas of 0.6 and 0.8 are PRICED in the sensitivity grid

kd.source: MARGINAL cost of debt, AED, forward-looking: du has ZERO drawn debt and no bonds (audited Note 4.2, all years; H1-2026: AED 2.0bn RCF undrawn), so the marginal rate is constructed: AED sovereign anchor 4.48% (Jan-2031 tranche) + ~60bp A/AA-range GCC telecom spread read from the stc (Aa3/A+) USD sukuk curve (4.63%/4.92%/5.17% at 2.8/4.4/9.4y vs matched UST, 06-Aug-2026) = 5.10%. Sits ABOVE the sovereign as required. The 3.6% IFRS-16 lease-implied rate (FY2025 lease interest 71.094 / average lease book 1,968.8) is the historical incremental-borrowing rate on the lease stock, disclosed for the record, NOT the marginal Kd

kd_term.source: Terminal marginal Kd: terminal AED sovereign 4.30% + 60bp telecom spread, rounded

rf_term.source: Terminal AED risk-free 4.30%: Fed long-run neutral ~3% (FOMC dots) implies a ~4.2-4.4% 10y UST through the term premium, and the AED curve prints at/through UST under the peg (Jan-31 tranche +4bp). Below the current 4.48% anchor - the glide is mild easing, not a heroic rate call. Markets currently price possible near-term HIKES (~4% policy by end-2026), which is why the glide is kept shallow

erp_term.source: Terminal ERP held at the rating-basis UAE ERP 4.87% (no structural convergence assumed for an Aa2 sovereign already near mature-market pricing)

wd_term.source: Terminal debt weight 5%: the disclosed capital structure is leases-only (~3.4% of EV at spot) and the board's stated posture is an unleveraged balance sheet with an undrawn RCF; 5% allows the lease book plus modest working facilities in perpetuity

rf_path.source: AED risk-free glide path FY2026->FY2030: linear from the 4.48% live anchor to the 4.30% terminal - the glide fractions for the forward WACC are THIS path's own cumulative progress (the cost-of-money path, since du carries no debt whose Kd could define the glide)

pe_just.source: Justified P/E 15.5x = the GCC-telecom peer median: e& 20.7x, stc 18.9x, Mobily 15.5x, Ooredoo ~12.5x, Omantel 11.4x, Zain ~9x (trailing, public aggregator reads 08/09-Aug-2026, labelled CROSS-CHECK). Mobily is the closest structural analogue (second operator, growth phase). du itself trades ~16.5x trailing

div_yield_peer.source: GCC telecom incumbent dividend-yield bracket ~4.8-6.7% (e& 4.8%, stc 5.2%, Omantel 6.7%, aggregator reads Aug-2026, cross-check label); 5.2% (stc, the regional benchmark payer) used as the yield-lens anchor

roe_sust.source: Sustainable ROE 27%: audited ROE on average equity FY2023 18.5%, FY2024 26.0%, FY2025 29.0% - the step-up is the 2024 regime change (43.6% take vs 53.1%) plus operating leverage; 27% sits just below the FY2025 print and is consistent with the ~100% payout / 2.5% growth pair (implied retention 9%)

beta.index: DFM General Index (official DFM API + Yahoo splice, cross-validated)

composite_alt.note: equal-weight AE library composite, house cross-check construction

e3.method_short: cash returns vs cost of capital

assert_log: DU — ASSERT / derivation log (built on audited FY23-25 + reviewed Q1/H1-2026 filings)

[Historical income statement] FY2025 EBITDA 7,338 is PRINTED on the face ('operating profit before depreciation and amortization', IFRS 18); FY2024 comparative likewise (6,470). FY2023 predates IFRS 18 and prints no such line — the 5,800 carried here is DERIVED from audited components and flagged. Margins: FY23 42.5%, FY24 44.2%, FY25 46.1%; H1-2026 ACTUAL 49.2%.

[Fiscal regime] combined royalty+tax take: FY2023 53.1% (OLD regime: 15% of regulated revenue + 30% of regulated profit), FY2024 42.2%, FY2025 43.6% (CURRENT regime: 38% royalty + 9% CT, legislated 2024-2026 only). The post-2026 regime is THE CONTESTED JUDGEMENT — both framings are computed and published side by side.

[Working capital, audited, royalty-accrual-adjusted] FY23 -965 (-7.1% of revenue), FY24 -1,220 (-8.3%), FY25 -1,062 (-6.7%) — structurally NEGATIVE, the classic prepaid/deferred-revenue telecom shape: customers and payables fund the operation. Cycle: DSO 51d (FY23 60d), payables 85d of revenue, inventory 5d of direct costs. The forecast holds the FY2025 component days constant, so NWC stays -6.7% of revenue and GROWTH RELEASES cash rather than absorbing it.

[Balance sheet] ZERO drawn borrowings in every year studied (Note 4.2 prints Total borrowings '–'); cash + term deposits: FY23 1,937, FY24 2,283, FY25 2,250. Lease liabilities (the only debt-like item): FY23 2,105 -> FY25 1,939. Net cash AFTER leases at FY2025: +311.
[Segment contribution margins FY24] mobile 60.9%, fixed 84.6%, wholesale 88.0%, ict 20.8%
[Segment contribution margins FY25] mobile 60.8%, fixed 85.8%, wholesale 86.4%, ict 19.4%

[Unit-build reconciliation, FY2025] avg mobile base 9,310k x ARPU AED 63.3 x 12 = 7,072 vs disclosed mobile segment revenue 7,075 (-0.0%) — the subscribers-x-ARPU frame reproduces the audited segment to within a percent.
[Revenue build] FY26E 16,593 (+4.3% vs guidance 4-6% revised 23-Jul-2026) -> FY30E 19,424. Segments FY26E: mobile 7,209, fixed 4,806, wholesale 2,548, ict 2,031

[EBITDA — an OUTPUT, not an input] 7,822 (47.1%) -> 8,117 (47.1%) -> 8,481 (47.1%) -> 8,815 (47.1%) -> 9,132 (47.0%). H1-2026 actual margin was 49.2% and H2 is seasonally softer (H2-2025: 45.2%); the FY26E output sits against the company's 46-47% guidance — ABOVE it, because H1 already printed 49.2% and the build holds disclosed contribution margins rather than forcing the guidance midpoint.
[D&A roll-forward] FY26E 2,235 (2x reviewed H1-2026 actual = 2,266 — within 1.4%); PP&E 10,289 -> 12,432.

[Cost of equity] rf 4.48% (Jan-2031 AED T-bond) less UAE rating-basis default spread 0.42% = rf* 4.06%; + beta 0.472 x ERP 4.87% -> Ke 6.36%. ERP basis 2 (market-spread, implied-US base): 6.43%. RETIRED un-netted construction 6.78% (audit trail only).

[WACC explicit] weights: lease debt 3.4% / market equity 96.6% (market cap 55,755; du has no drawn borrowings) -> WACC 6.24% (basis 2: 6.31%). Interest shields both fiscal legs (the royalty base is profit AFTER interest), so the shield runs at the combined 43.6%.
[WACC terminal] Ke 6.18%; Kd after tax 2.77%; weights 95%/5% -> 6.01%
[Terminal] ROIC(term) 26.7%; reinvestment = g/ROIC = 9.4% of NOPAT; TV 97,871 at g 2.5% / WACC(term) 6.01%

[DCF] PV(explicit) 12,362 + PV(terminal) 72,697 (TV = 85% of EV) = EV 85,059; − leases 1,939 + cash & deposits 2,250 + investees 0.5 = equity 85,370 -> AED 18.83 at 31-Dec-2025; x accretion 1.0377 − final dividend 0.40 paid 28-Apr-2026 = AED 19.14 at the 07-Aug-2026 anchor

[Contested judgement — BOTH WAYS] Framing A (regime persists, 43.6% take): AED 19.14. Framing B (reversion to the pre-2024 construction, effective take 51.5% -> 51.7%): AED 16.29. Gap +2.85/share (-15%). Published side by side; never averaged.
[rf tenor gap, PRICED] 10y peg-extrapolated rf 4.69% instead of the Jan-2031 AED print 4.48% -> WACC 6.44% -> AED 18.09 (-1.05/share)
[DCF scenarios] bear 10.97 / base 19.14 / bull 29.58 AED per share

[Relative lens] trailing P/E 19.2x, trailing EV/EBITDA 7.6x (du's own, computed from audited figures). Justified P/E 15.5x (GCC peer median) x FY26E EPS 0.70 -> AED 11.20 at the anchor [bear 12x 8.67 / bull 18.5x 13.36]. Dividend-yield cross: DPS 0.68 / peer benchmark 5.2% = AED 13.12. Peer EV/EBITDA was NOT reliably sourceable from public aggregators (flagged) — the relative lens runs on P/E and yield, both sourced.
[Normalised lens] mid-cycle margin 47.1% (FY2028E) on FY2026E revenue -> normalised EPS 0.69 x 15.5 = AED 11.18 at the anchor

[Book lens] justified P/B = (27% − 2.5%) / (6.18% − 2.5%) = 6.66x on BVPS 2.24 -> AED 15.47 at the anchor. A 27% sustainable ROE against a 6.2% cost of equity is what a licensed duopoly with negative working capital looks like; the multiple is high because the equity base is small, not because the claim is aggressive. Trailing ROE 29.0%.
[Synthesis] weighted central AED 15.20; span 8.65 - 29.58; spot 12.30 (+24% to the central).
